sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Gorinchem, a fortified town on the Merwede, charges for parking inside its ramparts and has seen a controversial rise in rates. The council adopted the fourth amendment of the parking ordinance on 16 December 2025, with the 2026 tariff table from 1 January: 2.00 euros an hour in the Kweeklust and Kazerneplein garages, 3.32 euros an hour for other streets inside the ramparts, 4.16 euros at Groenmarkt and 1.66 euros on the outer car parks Paardenwater and Buiten de Waterpoort, and the fine rose from 78.80 to 82.00 euros [0][14]. A D66 council question of December 2024 described the rise from 1 January 2025 as a regular 10 percent index plus an extra 30 percent, taking street parking from 2.30 to 3.22 euros and garages from 1.38 to 1.93 euros, with extra revenue of about 1 million euros a year and a letter of concern from the city-centre traders; these are D66's numbers [3]. In the lower town paid parking runs from 10:00 to 22:00 Monday to Saturday and, newly, 12:30 to 17:00 on Sundays, in the upper town from 10:00 to 24:00 every day, and in the garages from 10:00 to 17:00, Thursday until 20:00, under a decision of December 2024 that may since have been revised [2]. A first resident permit costs 98.60 euros a year, a second 505.70 euros and a business permit 629.55 euros [1]. A policy of December 2025 sets exemptions for the car-restricted centre, a pedestrian zone including Groenmarkt, Grote Markt and Hoogstraat, for loading, for people who can reasonably only be fetched or brought by vehicle, and for reaching private parking [15].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: Planning is about the station and old programmes. The parking programme for the centre for 2021 to 2025 aimed at no more than 80 percent average occupancy of street spaces and recorded night-time street occupancy above 90 percent, locally over 100 percent, in the southern parts of both towns; its measures were mostly studies of expanding Kweeklust and Bagijnenwal, of residents using Kazerneplein and of the guidance system, and we found no later version [7][9]. It also found a need for 95 public charging posts [10]. In a committee session in June 2025 councillors discussed the draft framework for the station area, which proposed the lowest possible parking norm for new homes and offices, while one councillor asked what would happen to the large Q-Park facility at the station that 'is usually not used' and another why so little use is made of the park-and-ride; these are remarks and not measurements [12][13]. A traffic decision of November 2025 covers the reconstruction of Banneweg and Stationsweg with a new roundabout and moves the entry of the Stadhuisplein car park [17]. A decision of April 2025 designates extra charging bays at four neighbourhood sites [6].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The municipality runs the Kweeklust and Kazerneplein garages itself, behind barriers with payment on exit, while the three outer car parks have no barriers and payment in advance [9]. A presentation to the council in September 2024 put parking revenue at about 2.61 million euros against costs of about 1.59 million, a balance of about 1.02 million euros, without saying whether these were actuals or a forecast, and compared Gorinchem's garage rate with Tiel at 1.80 euros, Gouda at 2.00 and Dordrecht at 1.50 to 2.75, against 1.38 in Gorinchem then [4][5]. The same presentation put the Q-Park at the station at 1.53 euros an hour [5]. The register and Q-Park both list the P+R Stationsweg with 127 spaces, open round the clock, operated by Nederlandse Spoorwegen according to the register, whose tariff entry of 1.46 euros an hour is from June 2021 and may be out of date [11][16].

Our data cover the P+R Stationsweg, with 127 spaces, for about 38 days since late August 2026. Occupancy averaged about 8% on weekdays and 4% at weekends, and peaked at 45% around midday on a Thursday, so it is almost always nearly empty. The garages are not in our data.
